title: Zangarmarsh
body: Zangarmarsh is a vast wetland in western Outland, where mushrooms taller than any tree rise over still pools and glowing fungi light the gloom, and even the giants that wade the bogs are made of living fungus. The druids of the Cenarion Expedition came expecting small pockets of life and found a thriving wilderness; then they noticed the water falling. Draenei, Broken and Lost Ones, Darkspear trolls, sporelings, ogres and naga all share the marsh.

title: Cenarion Refuge
body: The Cenarion Refuge in the east of the marsh is the headquarters of the Cenarion Expedition, led by the night elf druid Ysiel Windsinger. Two great ancients stand among its buildings, and its wardens guard against the naga, who have attacked the druids since the day they arrived, in strength and numbers no one foresaw. A Broken who escaped slavery among the Lost Ones teaches the druids what he knows of the land.

parts.body: The first answer to the falling water came from Umbrafen Lake: a steam pump worked by the naga, drawing the lake away. At last the druids understood the naga's hostility.
sources: quest 9912 description (main path west from Cenarion Post leads to the refuge in eastern Zangarmarsh)

parts.body: Flown over every great lake in stormcrow shape, Ysiel's scout confirmed her fears: the naga have set up pumping stations at all the major lakes of Zangarmarsh.

title: Serpent Lake
body: Serpent Lake spreads across the north of the marsh. On its eastern shore the Bloodscale naga work the lake's own steam pump with Wrekt slaves, and beneath its water lies Coilfang Reservoir, the naga's stronghold, its great cavern opening on slave pens, the Underbog and the steam vaults, and deeper still a shrine of the serpent.

parts.body: Schematics taken from the naga show a hidden network of drains linking the marsh's lakes to a giant drain at the center of Serpent Lake: a sink for all of Zangarmarsh.
sources: quest 9731 description and reward text (drains and pumps connect the lakes to Serpent Lake, giant drain in the center, water sink)

parts.body: The druids Ysiel sent to investigate the drain never returned. One waits at the reservoir's entrance with a twisted ankle; his companions went on inside.

title: Telredor
body: Telredor is built atop a giant mushroom in the east of the marsh, its halls lit by cultivated spores, since little in the swamp will burn. For centuries it was a secluded retreat for draenei priests; when the orcs began attacking the draenei, Anchorite Ahuurn turned it into a haven to which many owe their lives. Today it is the Alliance's stronghold in the marsh, and Ahuurn longs to welcome even the Lost Ones back among their people.

parts.body: The Feralfen elder Kuruti refused his envoy: his people want nothing from the draenei who turned their backs on them, least of all a redemption offered through trickery.

title: Orebor Harborage
body: In the ruins of an old draenei temple northwest of Serpent Lake a small band of Broken has made a home: the Kurenai, who wish to reunite with their draenei kin, sent from their city of Telaar in Nagrand under Ikuti to strengthen ties with Telredor. They are wary of strangers, for wariness has kept them alive, and one of them senses that the temple once meant something to him.

parts.body: One of them was once a slave himself, and the Kurenai are ashamed to be too few to free their brethren still toiling at the naga's pumps.

title: Zabra'jin
body: Zabra'jin is the Darkspear town in the west of the marsh, overseen by Shadow Hunter Denjai, who also sent a crew east to build Swamprat Post on the eastern border. The town is hemmed in, by Ango'rosh ogres cutting their way toward its walls from the north and by Lost One assassins of the Daggerfen tribe on the roads, and a messenger from Garadar has come begging for help.

parts.body: Plans taken from the Ango'rosh camp prove Denjai right: the ogres' cutting so close to his walls was no accident, but the preparation for an attack on Zabra'jin.

title: Sporeggar
body: Sporeggar is the village of the sporelings, a small and mostly peaceful people, grown from tallstalk mushrooms between Sporewind and Marshlight Lakes; glowcap mushrooms serve them as coin. Their young grow in spore sacs at the Spawning Glen to the south, and lately starving bog lords have been crossing the road to devour them. A fungal giant, Fhwoor, lives among the sporelings, for they saved him long ago.

parts.body: The bog lords' hunger has a cause: the Ango'rosh ogres are cutting down the mushrooms of the Hewn Bog where the giants used to feed.

title: The Dead Mire
body: The Dead Mire, northeast of Telredor, is a stretch of cracked and parched ground where the marsh has dried away and almost everything living withers. Withered giants stalk it, attacking anything in their path, and no one who has ventured in has ever reported seeing anything alive and well there.

parts.body: The mire was once one of the marsh's lakes and the spawning ground of the fungal giants. With the water gone they can no longer spore, and if nothing changes they may disappear entirely.
